Hostname update:The Qubrid platform is now at qubrid.com. [Read the migration guide](https://docs.platform.qubrid.com/inferencing/Migration)

The API Key Generation feature allows you to securely access and interact with Qubrid serverless models and the OpenAI-compatible API on the Qubrid AI Platform. This key enables seamless integration into external apps, tools, or workflows via API requests - empowering you to run model queries programmatically.

You should be logged in the Qubrid AI Platform in order to generate an API Key

## [How to generate an API Key?](https://docs.platform.qubrid.com/Manage%20API%20Keys\#how-to-generate-an-api-key)

1

#### Go to API Keys

Navigate to the top navbar of the Qubrid AI Platform dashboard and click on API Keys.

2

#### Create new API Key

Click on Create API Key button and generate your API Key

3

#### Add Details

Provide a name and description for your API Key to help you identify its purpose later.
You can also set expiration date for the key if needed.

4

#### Save and View Key

You will see a pop-up with your newly created API Key

Important: Please copy and securely store your API key. It will only be displayed once upon generation. If you lose this key, you will need to regenerate a new one.

## [What Are API Keys?](https://docs.platform.qubrid.com/Manage%20API%20Keys\#what-are-api-keys)

**API Keys** are unique identifiers that allow you to authenticate and securely access the Qubrid Platform APIs.

They are required when you want to interact with the platform programmatically - for example, to launch GPU instances, deploy models, or run inference from your own applications.

#### [Key Points](https://docs.platform.qubrid.com/Manage%20API%20Keys\#key-points)

- **Authentication**: Every API request must include a valid API key to verify your identity.
- **User-Specific**: Keys are tied to your account or organization. You can generate multiple keys if needed.
- **Permissions**: API keys inherit your account permissions (e.g., project access, team role).
- **Security**: Keep your API keys private. Never share them publicly or commit them to version control.

#### [Typical Use Cases](https://docs.platform.qubrid.com/Manage%20API%20Keys\#typical-use-cases)

- Automating GPU instance creation.
- Deploying or managing AI templates and workflows via scripts.
- Running inference jobs directly from your application.
- Integrating Qubrid into CI/CD pipelines.

## [API Logs](https://docs.platform.qubrid.com/Manage%20API%20Keys\#api-logs)

Review inference activity, debug failed requests, and track token usage and cost from the platform.

1

#### Open API Logs

In the left menu on the [Qubrid AI Platform](https://qubrid.com/), click **API Logs**.

2

#### Select a model category

Choose the model category you want to inspect:

**Text** or **Code**.

3

#### Review log details

Each row shows:

- **Request Time**
- **Model Name**
- **Input Tokens**
- **Output Tokens**
- **TTFT** (time to first token)
- **Latency**
- **Status Code**
- **API Key** (first few characters, to identify which key was used)
- **Cost**

4

#### Move between pages

Use the **Previous** and **Next** buttons at the bottom of the table to switch pages when there are more logs than fit on one screen.

5

#### Filter logs

Open the **Filters** option to narrow results:

- **Status** \- show **Failed** or **Success** requests
- **Model** \- view logs for a specific model
- **Custom date** \- limit logs to a date range you choose

API Logs are useful after you start calling models from the [Quickstart API](https://docs.platform.qubrid.com/inferencing/Quickstart%20API), integrations, or your own applications. Cross-check unexpected costs or errors against the key prefix shown in each row.
